distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 0.0672 +/- 0.0098 mas (same row, RUWE 1.08): 14887.92 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 53.179 (49.564 to 57.846) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 36,996,818 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 4.998 (4.958 to 5.202) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 4602 +/- 91.9 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 6363141971994511360: teff_gspphot 4601.8013 K (16th-84th percentiles 4528.883-4712.78), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 6363141971994511360: teff_gspphot 4601.8013 K (16th-84th percentiles 4528.883-4712.78), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/gaia-dr3-6363141971994511360.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 1.685, rounded to two decimals
